title: gdacs-fl-1104081 is the sole and unbroken occupant of run.json's overdue_drift list across all 39 nights the field has existed, and it is also the only one of 113 GDACS eventids preserved in this observatory's full record whose reported episodeid has ever run backward
statement: sensor-cold-start-overdue-drift.json was promoted on 2026-08-14 on the strength of one case, gdacs-fl-1104081, and the sensor's own not_promoted-turned-promoted evidence only covered two nights (2026-08-13, 2026-08-14). Scanning every foreknown/snapshots/<date>/run.json that carries an overdue_drift field -- 39 nights, 2026-08-09 through 2026-09-21 -- finds that field has named exactly one future, gdacs-fl-1104081, on 37 of those 39 nights, and has never named any other future at any point; the two exceptions (2026-08-31, 2026-09-06) are both empty lists rather than a different member, and both are nights on which foreknown/registry.json's own history for this same future records a REVISED event extending its window (2026-08-31T11:49:28, 2026-09-06T09:39:02). Independently, extracting properties.episodeid for every (eventid, night) pair across all 40 preserved foreknown/snapshots/<date>/gdacs.json files (2026-08-08 through 2026-09-21) and checking each of the 113 distinct eventids for a night-over-night decrease finds exactly one such decrease in the observatory's entire preserved GDACS record, and it belongs to the same future: gdacs-fl-1104081's own episodeid read 14 on 2026-08-28, 2026-08-29 and 2026-08-30 (the feature's iscurrent read 'false' on the third of those nights, 2026-08-30, while still being the only feature present for eventid 1104081), then read 11 on 2026-08-31 -- one of the two nights overdue_drift went empty -- before resuming its climb the following nights (12 on 09-01, 13 on 09-02, 15 on 09-03, 17 on 09-06, ..., 19 on 09-21, the newest snapshot). No other tracked eventid, across 113 checked, shows episodeid move anything but forward or stay flat between consecutive preserved nights.
method: Loaded every foreknown/snapshots/<date>/run.json (2026-08-08 through 2026-09-21) that contains an overdue_drift key and recorded its full value per night (39 nights found; 37 read ['gdacs-fl-1104081'], 2 read []). Cross-checked the two empty nights (2026-08-31, 2026-09-06) against foreknown/registry.json's gdacs-fl-1104081.history for a same-date REVISED event and confirmed both match exactly, while the future's other seven REVISED dates (2026-08-17, 08-21, 08-25, 08-28, 09-03, 09-15, 09-21) do not coincide with an empty overdue_drift list. Separately, loaded every foreknown/snapshots/<date>/gdacs.json (40 nights present, one gap at 2026-08-27), grouped every feature by properties.eventid (113 distinct ids across the full record), and for each id's per-night properties.episodeid sequence checked whether any value was lower than the immediately preceding preserved night's value for that same id; exactly one such instance exists in the whole record (gdacs-fl-1104081, 2026-08-31: 14 -> 11). Extracted gdacs-fl-1104081's full episodeid/datemodified/iscurrent trace across all 38 nights it has appeared (first seen 2026-08-12, matching its NOTARIZED date) to confirm the drop was a single isolated night, not a sustained reversal, and that the value resumed climbing past its pre-drop level (14) by 2026-09-03 (15). python -m pip install -e ./practice, python -m pytest practice/tests (185 passed, unchanged from obs-2026-09-20-1.json), python stage/generate.py --repo-root . and python verify.py --repo-root . run after appending this observation; all green.
worth_watching_because: The cold-start/drift split (sensor-cold-start-overdue-drift.json) has run for 39 nights and open_total has ranged from 93 to 139 futures over that span, yet drift_overdue has never had a second member and this one member has never left it for more than a single night. A sensor whose fired class has held exactly one name for its entire life is not yet distinguishable, from the committed record alone, between 'this correctly and rarely catches a genuine pattern' and 'this measures something specific to one record's own behaviour that happens to satisfy the definition, not a general phenomenon the definition was meant to generalise to.' The episodeid regression sharpens which record that is: gdacs-fl-1104081 is now independently unusual on two unrelated axes derived from two different code paths (overdue_kind() in futures.py for the first, the raw feed's own episodeid for the second), and the one night its episodeid ran backward is also one of only two nights it has ever dropped out of overdue_drift. sensor-source-ref-episode-drift.json's promoted test_rule reads 'current' episodeid from only the newest preserved snapshot on each run; this observation shows that value is not guaranteed monotonic even at the source, so a single night's drift-gap figure for this future in particular could read lower than a night either side of it, not just lower than its true historical maximum.
left_alone: Not proposing a redesign of sensor-cold-start-overdue-drift.json's test_rule: 39 nights of a single-member class is a fact about the committed record so far, not proof the class is malformed, and the falsification clause already names the condition (class stays empty by construction) that would argue for dropping it -- that has not happened either, since the class is non-empty on 37 of 39 nights. Not filing a review entry against sensor-cold-start-overdue-drift.json itself, since its definition, test_rule and falsification make no claim about how many distinct futures should occupy the class; a one-member class is consistent with what it was written to measure. Did add a short review note to sensor-source-ref-episode-drift.json (see this pass's diff) limited to the single new fact this observation established -- 'current' episodeid can regress at the source -- since that sensor's test_rule explicitly reads a single night's current value and its falsification clause did not previously name this possibility; the review does not change the sensor's code, threshold or status. Not re-deriving why GDACS's own episodeid briefly went backward for this event -- that would be a claim about the world, not the record. Not re-checking sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json or sensor-drought-window-class-crossing.json tonight beyond confirming via autonomy/log.jsonl that both continue posting their usual figures with no new values. No memoryhole verdicts: memoryhole/readings/2026-09-20.json, the newest reading, carries zero rule-layer abstentions across all 53 entries. The 2026-09-20/2026-09-21 spike in notarized and closed counts (37 and 33 notarized, 31 closed on 09-21, both well above the ~7-14 typical range) was checked against foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-21/run.json's closed and notarized lists and is entirely NWS flood watch/warning churn across a handful of Midwest county offices (karx, kdvn, kepz, kiln, klot, kmkx, krlx) opening and closing together -- consistent with a single regional weather event moving through NWS's normal watch-to-warning-to-expiry lifecycle rather than an observatory-side irregularity, so not filed as its own observation.
